speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the vertigo you are experiencing—does the room feel like it is spinning around you, or do you feel like you are about to faint? Also, how long has this episode been lasting?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the sensation of spinning return if you roll over in bed or look up, and do you experience any ringing in your ears or hearing loss? I also need to know if you have any history of high blood pressure or diabetes.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any hearing loss or ringing in your ears associated with the vertigo? I need to rule out Meniere's disease or labyrinthitis.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any hearing loss or ringing in your ears, and does the vertigo recur with specific head movements like rolling over in bed? I need to distinguish between peripheral causes like BPPV or Meniere's and central causes like a stroke. REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike maneuver

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Positive, inducing nystagmus and reproducing patient’s symptoms of vertigo when head is turned to the left and laid back.

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive Dix-Hallpike maneuver strongly suggests Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). To confirm which ear is affected, does the vertigo and nystagmus occur only when turning to the left, or does it also happen when turning to the right?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies headaches, hearing loss, tinnitus, loss of consciousness or neurological deficits.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the Dix-Hallpike maneuver was positive only on the left side, this confirms Left Posterior Canal BPPV. DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
